description: I am I. You are U.
summary:
We developed FireSync, an interactive geospatial web application that ingests, harmonizes, and visualizes satellite active fire hotspot detections from NASA’s MODIS and VIIRS instruments.

FireSync directly addresses the challenge by standardizing divergent sensor attributes into a unified pipeline: aligning confidence scores into a consistent scale, preserving Near-Real-Time observations, and eliminating overpass redundancies through a ~1.1 km² spatiotemporal grid prioritizing peak Fire Radiative Power (FRP). The web interface pairs an interactive surveillance map—featuring bounding-box area drawing, direct coordinate navigation, and sensor stream toggling (Harmonized, MODIS, VIIRS)—with a multi-year burning activity calendar built with accessible thermal color ramps and filtered CSV export.

This is important because bridging MODIS’s historical baseline with VIIRS’s high-resolution precision eliminates sensor-origin discrepancies. It equips emergency managers, forestry officials, and climate scientists with a seamless, consistent time series to evaluate seasonal burning patterns, compare current fire severity against historical benchmarks, and deploy targeted interventions.https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1fWaAADsKJQERG8lfbzEEMvmtJomk8B5y/edit?usp=drivesdk&ouid=117138898524537394026&rtpof=true&sd=truehttps://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1fWaAADsKJQERG8lfbzEEMvmtJomk8B5y/edit?usp=drivesdk&ouid=117138898524537394026&rtpof=true&sd=true
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

FireSync is a geospatial analytics web platform that harmonizes and visualizes satellite active fire detections from NASA’s MODIS (Terra/Aqua) and VIIRS (Suomi-NPP/NOAA) instruments. It operates through an integrated two-part architecture:

  1. The Data Harmonization Pipeline:
    • Confidence Standardization: Translates continuous MODIS percentages (0–100%) into the categorical format used by VIIRS (<30%→’l’<30\% \rightarrow \text{'l'}<30%→’l’, 30–79%→’n’30\text{–}79\% \rightarrow \text{'n'}30–79%→’n’, ≥80%→’h’\ge 80\% \rightarrow \text{'h'}≥80%→’h’), while preserving raw confidence for scientific queries.
    • NRT Data Preservation: Retains Near-Real-Time observations without classification by setting missing type to -1 (undetermined) rather than discarding recent telemetry.
    • Spatiotemporal Grid Deduplication: Projects all observations into equal 0.01∘×0.01∘0.01^\circ \times 0.01^\circ0.01∘×0.01∘ (~1.1 km ×\times× 1.1 km) grid bins. Detections sharing the same acquisition date, diurnal cycle (daynight), and grid cell are resolved by sorting descending by Fire Radiative Power (FRP) and retaining the peak radiative emitter per cell.
    • Metadata Fusion: Combines sensor and platform into a unified tag: Instrument (Satellite).
    • Live Surveillance Map: Renders thermal hotspots scaled and colored by radiant temperature in Kelvin. Features:
      • Sensor Layer Toggling: Allows switching on/off or comparing between individual streams (Harmonized, MODIS 1 km, and VIIRS 375 m).
      • Marquee Area Drawing: Freehand bounding-box tool allowing users to drag a selection across any region, dynamically isolating hotspots, recalculating daily statistics strictly for that boundary, and downloading a region-specific CSV.
      • Coordinate Navigation HUD: Interactive LAT and LON inputs that auto-pan (flyTo) and drop an animated crosshair target beacon.
      • Hotspot Inspector: Displays district, state, country (via reverse geocoding), confidence category, and NASA fire classification types (0=Vegetation, 1=Volcano, 2=Static industrial, 3=Offshore, -1=Undetermined).
    • Burning Activity Calendar: Displays a multi-year matrix (2020–2026) and 365-day heatmaps using an accessible 5-tier thermal color ramp to reveal seasonal fire shifts (e.g., pre-monsoon forest fires vs. post-monsoon crop residue burning).
    • Historical Data Archive: Custom date-range filtering, benchmark presets, summary analytics, and full CSV dataset downloads.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Eliminates Sensor Incompatibilities: Users no longer need to manually reconcile different coordinate resolutions, conflicting confidence definitions, or duplicate overpasses between Terra, Aqua, and Suomi-NPP.
  • Instant Analytical Response: Over 3.28 million fire records are indexed locally in SQLite using compound B-Trees, returning spatial and temporal queries across the subcontinent in milliseconds without client-side memory overload.
  • Granular Fire Verification: Distinguishes true vegetation wildfires and stubble burning (Type 0) from persistent industrial heat sources like gas flares or steel mills (Type 2).
  • Ad-Hoc Regional Extraction: Emergency managers can define arbitrary administrative or natural boundaries with the area-draw marquee tool and export isolated CSV subsets immediately for ground deployment.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

  • Longitudinal Fire Ecology: Enables scientists and environmental policy makers to compare modern high-resolution fire data directly against multi-year historical baselines without sensor-switch distortions.
  • Seasonal Outbreak Preparedness: Equips state disaster management agencies and forestry departments with an accessible calendar to anticipate recurring fire peaks (such as Punjab/Haryana harvest residue burning in October–November and forest fire seasons in March–May).
  • Actionable Tactical Intelligence: Gives firefighters and local first responders clean, exportable fire coordinates with radiant brightness and radiative power metrics to evaluate fire severity and prioritize resource dispatch.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Programming Languages: Python 3 (Data engineering & Backend API), JavaScript / JSX (Frontend interface), SQL (Database querying).
  • Data Processing & Harmonization: Python (pandas, numpy, pathlib).
  • Database & Storage: SQLite3 with compound B-Tree indexes (idx_fires_search on acq_date & daynight).
  • Backend Architecture: Zero-dependency Python server using standard library http.server, sqlite3, and json for an ultra-lightweight deployment footprint.
  • Frontend Framework & Libraries: React 19, Vite, Leaflet, Lucide React, and html-to-image for high-resolution PNG snapshot capture.
  • Basemap Services: Esri World Imagery Satellite Cartography and OpenStreetMap.
  • Geocoding API: BigDataCloud reverse geocoding client API with offline geographic fallback.
  • Development & Version Control: Git, GitHub, Node.js & npm, PowerShell.

5. How is your project creative?

  • FRP-Prioritized Grid Fusion: Instead of simply averaging or discarding duplicate satellite passes, FireSync creates a ~1.1 km² spatial grid and uses Fire Radiative Power (MW) as the physical decision metric—ensuring peak thermal intensity is never diluted.
  • Dual-Mode Interactive Spatial Exploration: Combines two distinct ways to pinpoint fires: freehand marquee rectangle drawing for regional spatial bounding boxes, and an editable latitude/longitude HUD with animated camera navigation and pulsating crosshair beacons.
  • Perceptually Progressive Accessible Heatmaps: Bypasses traditional red-green color blind traps by using a monotonic luminosity-temperature scale (Light Yellow →\rightarrow→ Amber →\rightarrow→ Vibrant Orange →\rightarrow→ Deep Red →\rightarrow→ Dark Maroon) across the burning calendar matrix.
  • Direct Calendar-to-Surveillance Pivot: Clicking any cell in the 7-year burning calendar directly loads and inspects the live satellite overpasses for that specific day on the interactive map

    6. What factors did your team consider?
  • Near-Real-Time Data Preservation: Raw FIRMS NRT data lacks post-processed fire classification types. We filled missing types with -1 so current active fires remain visible rather than being dropped during data cleaning.
  • Accessibility for Diverse Users: Designed color scales that maintain contrast in grayscale and under red-green color blindness (deuteranopia/protanopia), ensuring fire charts are readable for all responders.
  • Contextual Reverse Geocoding: Satellite data provides raw coordinates; emergency responders think in terms of districts and states. We integrated live reverse geocoding to resolve lat/lon coordinates into administrative boundaries instantly.
  • Low-Bandwidth Ground Realities: Frontline responders often work in field conditions with constrained connectivity. We built a zero-dependency server, local SQLite storage, and chunked CSV streaming so the entire platform operates quickly without loading heavy megabyte-sized raw CSVs into client browser memory.
